members: [untitled BTM module] These genes mark the megakaryocyte-platelet arm of haematopoiesis and the signalling that supports it. Platelet factor 4 is the archetypal alpha-granule chemokine released on platelet activation, junction plakoglobin anchors the cytoskeletal junctions and desmosomal-type adhesion used by these cells, and the G protein alpha-z subunit couples platelet ADP and adrenergic receptors to inhibition of adenylate cyclase, lowering cyclic AMP to permit aggregation.

[untitled BTM module] These genes converge on receptor-proximal signalling that converts extracellular cues into changes in cell adhesion, migration and tissue remodelling. One arm is vascular and mesenchymal: endoglin acts as a TGF-beta superfamily co-receptor in endothelium, CCN2/CTGF and CRIM1 shape growth-factor availability in the matrix, and focal adhesion kinase with GAB1, PLCB1 and the Ral activator RGL1 relay integrin and growth-factor input to the cytoskeleton and to Ras-family GTPase output.

only_in_confusable: [untitled BTM module] These genes converge on myeloid and platelet function, where surface signalling is translated into changes in the actin cytoskeleton and in gene expression. The Src-family kinase LYN sits at the top of immunoreceptor and integrin signalling in leukocytes and platelets, setting both activating and inhibitory tone, while LST1 is an immune-cell transmembrane protein that shapes membrane protrusions and cell-cell contact.

[untitled BTM module] These genes mark a perivascular stromal and endothelial compartment, the interface where capillaries meet connective tissue matrix. Secreted matrix components such as EFEMP1 (fibulin-3) and ECM2 organise the basement membrane and elastic fibre environment that keeps vessels and surrounding tissue mechanically coherent, while IL33 acts both as a nuclear factor in endothelium and, when released from damaged cells, as an alarmin that recruits type 2 immune responses.

[untitled BTM module] These genes outline an endothelial identity and blood-vessel morphogenesis programme, of the kind that distinguishes vascular endothelium and sets arterial versus venous character during angiogenic remodelling. Its output is a patent, correctly patterned vascular network: guidance receptors such as neuropilin-1 and the fibronectin leucine-rich repeat protein FLRT2 read angiogenic and adhesive cues, adhesion-family GPCRs enriched in endothelium (ADGRL4/ELTD1, ADGRL2) tune sprouting behaviour, and the soluble guanylate cyclase alpha subunit places nitric oxide-cGMP signalling and vessel tone in the same module.
